539	### 2026-05-21 — Perf-logging bandwidth/capacity scoping
540	
541	Crunched numbers ahead of designing a frame-by-frame perf log (video + detector + actuator state) so we know which resolutions and which transports are actually in scope. Detail below; takeaway is that the spec's already-chosen "sparse keyframes + dense state" point (~1 MB/s) is the only real sweet spot, and the "full-rate raw video" wish is dead on arrival across every transport SAM9X75 has.
542	
543	**Baseline — 720×480 RGB888 (BGR888-packed in our pipeline) @ 60 Hz**
544	
545	- Per frame: 720 × 480 × 3 = **1.04 MB**.
546	- Per second: **62.2 MB/s ≈ 498 Mb/s**.
547	- All state payload (detector_state_t × 2 detectors + actuator + timing snapshot + per-frame metadata header) is ~150 B/frame ≈ **9 KB/s** — rounding error against pixels. This is a video-bandwidth problem, not a state-volume problem.
548	
549	**Scaled-down variants (per-second bandwidth)**
550	
551	| Variant | B/s |
552	|---|---|
553	| Full 720×480 RGB888 @ 60 Hz | 62.2 MB/s |
554	| Same @ 30 Hz | 31.1 MB/s |
555	| 720×480 RGB565 @ 60 Hz | 41.5 MB/s |
556	| 720×480 grayscale @ 60 Hz | 20.7 MB/s |
557	| 360×240 RGB888 @ 60 Hz | 15.6 MB/s |
558	| 360×240 RGB888 @ 30 Hz | 7.78 MB/s |
559	| 180×120 RGB888 @ 30 Hz | 1.94 MB/s |
560	| Strike-line strip 720×80 @ 60 Hz | 10.4 MB/s |
561	| 5 ROI patches 32×32 RGB888 @ 60 Hz | 922 KB/s |
562	| State-only (no pixels) @ 60 Hz | 9.1 KB/s |
563	
564	**Capacity over a session length**
565	
566	| Stream | 1 min | 5 min (song) | 10 min |
567	|---|---|---|---|
568	| Full @ 60 Hz | 3.73 GB | 18.7 GB | 37.3 GB |
569	| 360×240 @ 30 Hz | 467 MB | 2.33 GB | 4.67 GB |
570	| 1 keyframe/s + state (≈ spec §4.6) | 62 MB | 311 MB | 622 MB |
571	| ROI patches 60 Hz | 55 MB | 277 MB | 553 MB |
572	| State only | 547 KB | 2.7 MB | 5.5 MB |
573	
574	**Transport ceilings on this hardware** (sustained, realistic)
575	
576	| Channel | Sustained | Peripheral status |
577	|---|---|---|
578	| UART 115.2 kBd (console) | ~11 KB/s | in use (FLEXCOM4) |
579	| UART 921.6 kBd | ~92 KB/s | EDBG bridge cap |
580	| UART 3 Mbd (FLEXCOM max) | ~300 KB/s | unlikely through bridges |
581	| USB CDC ACM (HS device, class-stack overhead) | ~5–15 MB/s | device peripheral unused |
582	| USB Bulk (HS device, custom class) | ~30–40 MB/s | needs custom host-side reader |
583	| SDMMC Class-10 via FAT32 | ~5–10 MB/s | already planned for §4.6 keyframes |
584	| SDMMC UHS-I | ~25–50 MB/s | bus capable, FS overhead bites |
585	| GMAC Ethernet UDP | ~30–60 MB/s | GMAC unused |
586	| GMAC Ethernet TCP | ~10–20 MB/s | GMAC unused |
587	
588	**What fits where**
589	
590	- **State-only (9 KB/s)** fits everywhere including the console UART — no new transport needed if the goal is just "trace detector + timing + actuator decisions per frame."
591	- **ROI patches 60 Hz (~1 MB/s)** preserves everything cv_marvin_v1 actually samples; streams comfortably over USB CDC, fits an entire song on SD with room to spare.
592	- **1 keyframe/s + dense state (~1 MB/s)** is what spec §4.6 already commits to, fits any modern SD card, and survives over USB CDC or Ethernet.
593	- **Full 60 Hz (62 MB/s)** doesn't fit any transport sustained, *and* a 5-minute song at that rate is 18.7 GB — DOA.

648	### 2026-05-20 — USB CDC host attach: EDBG composite enumerates, CDC class driver now binds
649	
650	Picked up where the prior session left off — VBUS not asserting, no device detected. Closed both halves.
651	
652	**VBUS.** MCC's `DRV_USB_VBUSPowerEnable` callback is wired in the host driver but the host stack never invokes it on this build. Asserted the two VBUS GPIOs (`VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_Set` / `VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_Set`) directly from `APP_Initialize` ahead of consumer init and `USB_HOST_BusEnable`. EDBG immediately enumerates.
653	
654	**Class-driver binding.** Enumeration succeeded but the CDC attach handler never fired. Added per-interface descriptor logging inside `F_USB_HOST_UpdateDeviceTask` to see what was actually being matched. Output revealed VID `0x03EB` PID `0x2175` — an EDBG composite with five interfaces: HID/CMSIS-DAP, CDC ACM IAD pair (comm + data), vendor, MSC. The IAD passed TPL match and got assigned to the CDC driver, but the CDC instance still flipped to `STATE_ERROR` without our app-level handler ever seeing the attach.
655	
656	Root cause was inside Microchip's CDC class driver: `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign` (both single-interface and IAD paths) requires the comm interface to declare `bInterfaceProtocol == USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_AT_V250` (`0x01`). EDBG declares `0x00` (none) — functionally identical CDC ACM in practice; Linux/macOS accept either. The TPL/IAD pre-check passes (TPL wildcards subclass/protocol), the CDC driver gets the interface group, then immediately rejects it on the AT-V.250 check. The interrupt pipe never opens, the instance errors out, and the app-level listener stays silent.
657	
658	Fix: relaxed both checks to `(AT_V250 || NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC)`. After the patch the FBL log shows `CDC device attached, handle opened` and `c=Y` heartbeat as expected. Logged as patch #7 in the MCC re-apply list.
659	
660	Also tested a hypothesis from the prior session that `USB_HOST_Initialize` had to run *after* the EHCI/OHCI driver inits. With the diagnostic logging in place, MCC's emitted order (`USB_HOST_Initialize` → `Legato_Initialize` → driver inits) enumerates and binds the CDC IAD just as well — the host layer evidently looks up HCD interfaces lazily at `USB_HOST_BusEnable` time. Backed out the hand-edit; one fewer re-apply patch to maintain. Decision-log entry above.
661	
662	Diagnostic instrumentation stripped at the end of the session: the per-interface descriptor dump and enumeration state-change logger in `usb_host.c`, and the periodic OHCI/EHCI register heartbeat in `fretboard_link.c`. What remains on disk: the two `usb_host_cdc.c` protocol-relaxation lines (patch #7), the app-level VBUS asserts, and a minimal `USB_HOST_EVENT` printf so future host-stack drama still surfaces in the log.

668	First on-target test after the M2 actuator path landed. Symptoms: video stream not starting, USB ports unpowered, FBL heartbeat firing with `connected=N`. Boot stopped after `TC358743: probe starting`.
669	
670	Root cause: the USB MCC regen reordered SYS_Initialize so `MMU_Initialize` and `AIC_INT_Initialize` ran *after* `TC0_CH0_TimerInitialize`, `FLEXCOM6_TWI_Initialize`, and `XLCDC_Initialize`. With AIC initialized late, the FLEXCOM6 interrupt vector wasn't owned by the AIC when the first I²C transfer ran; `OSAL_SEM_Pend(transferDone, WAIT_FOREVER)` blocked forever waiting for an ISR that never fired. FBL stayed alive because it's pure FreeRTOS — no peripheral interrupt dependency.
671	
672	Fix: reverted SYS_Initialize order so MMU/AIC/WDT-disable run before TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC. Display + capture came back on first boot. Logged as patch #6 in the MCC re-apply list above.

1	# marvin HDMI → BGRX32 Capture Pipeline
2	
3	Authoritative configuration reference for the 720p60 HDMI capture path on SAM9X75. Every stage, every register bit that matters, with datasheet citations. When something breaks, start here before grepping code.
4	
5	**Status:** working as of 2026-05-02. Validated at **1280×720p60** and **720×480p60**, native BGRX32 in DDR, no CPU post-processing. The pipeline is resolution-agnostic — PFE crop, DMA size, and framebuffer offsets all scale from the TC358743-detected `{width, height}` automatically.
6	
7	Datasheet references are to **SAM9X7 Series DS60001813** (sections 48 = MIPI CSI / D-PHY, 49 = CSI2DC, 50 = ISC). TC358743 refs are to the Toshiba datasheet + mainline Linux `drivers/media/i2c/tc358743.c`.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Pipeline overview
12	
13	```
14	HDMI source (Pi 720p60 RGB)
15	        │
16	        ▼
17	TC358743 HDMI-to-CSI-2 bridge
18	  DT=0x24 RGB888, 2 lanes, 972 Mbps/lane, continuous-clock mode
19	        │
20	        ▼                          <── MIPI CSI-2 D-PHY
21	SAM9X75 DWC D-PHY RX Gen3
22	  HSFREQRANGE=0x0A (950–1000 Mbps band)
23	        │
24	        ▼                          <── 40-bit isc_data bus
25	CSI2DC (Demultiplexer Controller)
26	  VPCFGR: DT=0x24, VC=0, PA=0, RMS=0
27	  → demux_data = 0x00_00RRGGBB, one pixel per VP word
28	        │
29	        ▼                          <── 40-bit vp_data bus
30	ISC — Parallel Front End (PFE)
31	  PFE_CFG0: MIPI=1, BPS=FORTY, MODE=PROGRESSIVE, CONT=1, COLEN=1, ROWEN=1
32	  PFE_CFG1: COLMIN=0, COLMAX=W-1   (1279)
33	  PFE_CFG2: ROWMIN=0, ROWMAX=H-1   (719)
34	        │
35	        ▼                          <── sub420_data[39:0] (unmodified through ISC)
36	ISC — Rounding/Limiting/Packing (RLP)
37	  RLP_CFG: MODE=BYPASS (15)
38	  → rlp_data[31:0] = sub420_data[31:0] = 0x00RRGGBB
39	        │
40	        ▼                          <── rlp_data[31:0]
41	ISC — DMA Host
42	  DCFG: IMODE=PACKED32, YMBSIZE=BEATS32, CMBSIZE=BEATS32
43	  → stores 32-bit words to DDR; little-endian = B G R 00 = BGRX32
44	        │
45	        ▼
46	DDR3 framebuffer  (1280 × 720 × 4 = 3,686,400 B/frame)
47	  B G R 00  B G R 00  B G R 00  ...
48	```
49	
50	---
51	
52	## 2. Stage-by-stage configuration
53	
54	### 2.1 HDMI source
55	
56	- 1280×720p @ 60 Hz, RGB (not YCbCr), progressive.
57	- Any stable DVI/HDMI source works. Raspberry Pi with `/boot/firmware/config.txt` forced to `hdmi_group=1 hdmi_mode=4 hdmi_force_hotplug=1 hdmi_drive=2` is the known-good reference.
58	- Pixel rate: 74.25 MHz (standard CEA-861 VIC 4 / 720p60).
59	
60	Full-range vs limited-range is sender-controlled. TC358743's AVI InfoFrame carries whatever the source advertises; currently Pi sends limited-range, so peak values in DDR are `0xFE` not `0xFF`. EDID colorimetry overrides are a separate future task.
61	
62	### 2.2 TC358743 HDMI-to-CSI-2 bridge
63	
64	Driver: `firmware/marvin/default/src/tc358743.c`. Register values derived from mainline Linux `tc358743.c`.
65	
66	| Register | Value | Meaning |
67	|---|---|---|
68	| `PLLCTL` PRD=4, FBD=144 | PLL out = 972 MHz | `hsck = (27 MHz / PRD) × FBD` |
69	| `CSI_CONFW` lanes | 2 | 2 data lanes × 972 Mbps = 1.944 Gbps total (plenty for 720p60 RGB888's ~1.33 Gbps) |
70	| `CONFCTL` | 0x0007 | PCLK divider off, 3-byte pixel pack, no audio |
71	| `FIFOCTL` | 0x0176 | FIFO level 374 (kernel hardcodes at all rates) |
72	| `VI_MODE` | 0xE6 | RGB888 input, 16-bit HDMI RX side |
73	| `VI_REP`  | 0x00 | **No pixel replication / doubling** (critical — was 0x80 in earlier 480p test and caused 16-row phase drift) |
74	| `VOUT_SET2` / `VOUT_SET3` | 0x01 / 0x08 | Output color format / range handling |
75	| CSI-2 DT | 0x24 | RGB888 per CSI-2 spec |
76	
77	D-PHY timing (for 972 Mbps):
78	```
79	LINEINITCNT  = 0x1B58
80	LPTXTIMECNT  = 0x0007
```

109	### 2.4 CSI2DC — the RMS=0 lever
110	
111	**This is the key decision that enables in-pipeline BGRX32.** DS60001813 §49.6.54:
112	
113	| VPCFGR Field | Value | Reason |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| DT (bits 5:0) | 0x24 | RGB888 (matches TC358743 emission) |
116	| VC (bits 7:6) | 0 | Virtual channel 0 |
117	| PA (bit 14) | **0** | LSB-aligned. PA=1 is for 10/12-bit Bayer sensors being packed onto ISC's 12-bit internal bus. Irrelevant for MIPI RGB888 bypass. |
118	| **RMS (bit 13)** | **0** | **Critical.** See below. |
119	| RGB36MAP (bit 15) | 0 | Use Table 49.25 pixel mapping |
120	
121	`RMS` (Recommended Memory Storage) per datasheet:

37	The SAM9X75 XLCDC BASE layer has **no window position or size registers** (`XLCDC_SetupBaseLayer` in `plib_xlcdc.c` configures `BASECFG0..BASECFG6` but no XPOS/YPOS/XSIZE/YSIZE). Pointing BASE at a 720-wide framebuffer while the display is 800 wide produces an 80 px/row skew because LCDC reads 800 × 4 = 3200 B/row but memory only has 720 × 4 = 2880 B/row — each row drifts left.
38	
39	Overlays (OVR1, OVR2, HEO) have `OVRxCFG2` (XPOS/YPOS) and `OVRxCFG3` (XSIZE/YSIZE), so their window can be smaller than the panel and positioned anywhere. OVR1 is the simplest overlay (no scaling, no chroma key). That's what we use.
40	
41	### 2.2 `XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_ARGB_8888`
42	
43	Our memory layout is `B G R X` (low-to-high), i.e. `0x00RRGGBB` as a little-endian 32-bit word.
44	
45	The MCC XLCDC enum exposes only `ARGB_8888` and `RGBA_8888`. Per SAM9X75 LCDC convention:
46	
47	| Mode | Memory byte order (low → high) |
48	|---|---|
49	| `ARGB_8888` | **B, G, R, A** |
50	| `RGBA_8888` | A, B, G, R |
51	
52	`ARGB_8888` is byte-for-byte compatible with our BGRX32 output. The `A` byte in memory ends up being our `X = 0x00`, which would mean fully transparent — but we override at the layer level:
53	
54	### 2.3 Global alpha via `XLCDC_SetLayerOpts(layer, 255, true, false)`
55	
56	OVR1's layer opts take a global alpha (0–255) and an `enable_dma` flag. We pass `alpha = 255` + `enable_dma = true`:
57	- `enable_dma = true` → pixel data comes from the framebuffer via DMA (RGB channels only).
58	- `alpha = 255` → the layer is fully opaque regardless of the per-pixel A byte.
59	
60	So our `X = 0x00` in the framebuffer is harmless; the display shows opaque RGB.
61	
62	### 2.4 Pillarbox, not scale
63	
64	Panel is 1280×800. Source dimensions vary; `lcd_bind_capture(w, h)` centers the source via `xpos = (1280-w)/2`, `ypos = (800-h)/2`. Common cases:
65	
66	| Source | Window | Pillarbox L+R | Letterbox T+B |
67	|---|---|---|---|
68	| 720×480 (Wii / Pi 480p) | 720×480 at (280, 160) | 280 px each | 160 px each |
69	| 1280×720 (Pi 720p) | 1280×720 at (0, 40) | 0 (fills width) | 40 px each |
70	
71	No scaling engine needed for either. BASE layer (below OVR1 in z-order) paints the surrounding black region — it's still the MCC-auto-allocated 1280×800 buffer of zeroes.
72	
73	If the source is larger than 1280×800 (e.g. 1080p), `lcd_bind_capture` bails with `LCD: source exceeds panel` and the bind step is skipped (capture pipeline still runs into DDR, just nothing on screen). Downscaling a > 1280×800 source requires the HEO layer's hardware scaler, which the MCC plib does not expose — it'd need direct `HEOCFG*` register writes. Deferred until needed.
74	
75	### 2.5 Single-buffer read, tear-tolerant
76	
77	XLCDC DMA re-reads the OVR1 base address on each of its own frame refreshes (60 Hz panel). We point it at **buffer 0** of the double-buffer pool (`ISC_Capture_GetBufferAddress()` returns the pool base = buffer 0). ISC DMA alternates writes between buffer 0 and buffer 1, so about half the captured frames are only visible to the CPU/vision stage, not to the display.
78	
79	Practical effect: display effective refresh is ~30 Hz (every other ISC write) and a scanline-level tear is possible where an LCDC read crosses mid-frame an ISC write. Good enough for a sanity check and for static/slow content. Upgrades when needed:
80	- **Synchronized pointer swap:** on ISC frame-done ISR, call `XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(OVR1, just_filled_buffer, true)`. The "update" flag delays the effect until the next panel VSYNC, so no mid-frame read tear.
81	- **Single-buffer capture:** set `iscObj->dmaDescSize = 1`. ISC overwrites the same buffer continuously; display tracks it at full 60 Hz with some scanline tear but no frame drop.
82	
83	---
84	
85	## 3. Cache coherency
86	
87	`g_framebuffer` lives in `.region_cache_aligned` (cached DDR). Consumers should read it like this:
88	
89	- **CPU does not write to the buffer** → no flush needed. ISC DMA writes bypass CPU cache and go straight to DDR; LCDC DMA reads straight from DDR. Both see the same data.
90	- **If CPU (vision, overlay rendering, alpha stamp) ever writes to the buffer** → call `SYS_CACHE_CleanDCache_by_Addr((uint32_t *)addr, size)` before yielding to LCDC, and `SYS_CACHE_InvalidateDCache_by_Addr` before reading something that DMA wrote.
91	
92	MCC's `drv_gfx_xlcdc.c` places its own auto-allocated buffers in `.region_nocache` to sidestep this entirely. We don't need that for a read-only display, but it's the standard pattern for CPU-rendered content.
93	
94	---
95	
96	## 4. Call sequence
97	
98	All wiring is in `firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c`:
99	
100	### 4.1 Boot-time (`APP_Initialize`)
101	
102	```c
103	XLCDC_EnableBacklight();
104	```
105	
106	MCC's auto-initialization (`SYS_Initialize`) already ran:
107	- `XLCDC_Initialize()` — clocks, timing engine, all 4 layers (BASE/OVR1/HEO/OVR2) set up at 1280×800 with auto-allocated buffers in `.region_nocache` (now in RGB565, ~2 MB per layer).
108	- `XLCDC_Start()` — panel clock, sync, disp enable, SD enable (all called from inside `Initialize`).
109	- `LVDSC_Initialize()` — LVDS serializer.
110	- `DRV_GFX2D_Initialize()` — 2D graphics engine (available for later work).
111	
112	Backlight is *not* turned on by auto-init. We do it ourselves.
113	
114	### 4.2 Per-capture (`app_coordinate_capture` → `lcd_bind_capture`)
115	
116	Runs once when TC358743 reports a lock and `ISC_Capture_Configure(w, h)` succeeds:
117	
118	```c
119	XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, false, true);
120	XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_ARGB_8888, false);
121	XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, ISC_Capture_GetBufferAddress(), false);
122	XLCDC_SetLayerXStride(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, 0u, false);
123	XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYPos(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, (800-w)/2, (480-h)/2, false);
124	XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYSize(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, w, h, false);
125	XLCDC_SetLayerOpts(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, 255u, true, false);
126	XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_OVR1, true, true);
127	```
128	
129	Note the `update = false` on all but the last call. The last `SetLayerEnable(true, true)` commits the pending config atomically, so the layer doesn't briefly render with a mix of old/new settings.
130	
131	`XStride = 0` means "no extra bytes between rows" — source memory is tightly packed at `window_width × 4 B/row`. If we later consume a buffer wider than the window (e.g. cropping a 1280×720 source down to an 800-wide visible strip), XStride would be `(source_width - window_width) × 4`.
132	
133	---
134	
135	## 5. Current limitations / next steps
136	
137	- **Panel-exceeding sources aren't displayed.** Pi 720p (1280×720) now fits the 1280×800 panel; only 1080p and beyond would need HEO scaling.
138	- **No double-buffer swap** — LCDC stuck on buffer 0, ~30 Hz effective with possible tear. Switch to ISR-driven pointer swap when motion clarity matters.
139	- **BASE layer is still the MCC-auto-allocated 1280×800 black buffer.** ~2 MB of `.region_nocache` DDR (RGB565) permanently displaying black around our overlay. Low priority; could reclaim by dropping `XLCDC_BUF_PER_LAYER` to 0 for BASE, or by disabling BASE entirely (the surrounding region would then go transparent and show whatever the LCDC's "default layer color" is — `BASECFG3.RDEF/GDEF/BDEF = 0,0,0`, i.e. black, same result).
140	- **Limited→full range expansion — will be done in the HEO CSC block, display-only.** TC358743 reports RGB limited-range (16–235) for both Wii and Pi sources, so bytes in DDR reflect that range. Vision consumers deliberately see **unexpanded** bytes — the 15% extra dynamic range of full scale doesn't carry any real information from a limited-range source (it's just a linear rescale), and keeping capture pristine means vision algorithms operate on ground-truth values. The expansion is cosmetic, needed only because the AC69T88A panel expects full 0–255 and would render limited-range data with muted blacks and washed-out whites.
141	  - **Chosen path:** HEO layer Color Space Conversion matrix (`HEOCFG14..17` on this chip). Programmable `out = M × in + offset` configured as an identity RGB→RGB with the correct gain/offset for the 219-step expansion. Zero CPU, happens at display time only, capture framebuffer unchanged.
142	  - Rejected alternatives: CPU LUT pass (burns cycles, and would either expand the capture buffer in place — breaking vision — or require a second buffer), GFX2D blit (not clear the engine has a linear gain mode at all).
143
```
</details></tool-use>

371	#### 4.6.6 On-device buffering
372	
373	A FreeRTOS task (`record_task`) owns SD writes. State / command / ADC streams are small and write through directly. Keyframes are larger — a single keyframe at 1.38 MB cannot block the video pipeline, so the record task receives a **frame buffer pointer** (the same DDR buffer the ISC writes into; refcounted by the video task) and writes from DDR while the next frame is being captured into another buffer. We need ≥ 3 capture frame buffers (one capturing, one displaying, one being recorded) when recording is active; today the video task already has multiple frames pre-allocated — exact count is verified during implementation.
374	
375	If the SD write FIFO falls behind (rare; only a sustained-throughput problem), the recorder drops keyframes (logs a `RECORD_DROP` event into `state.bin`'s metadata channel) but **never** drops detector-state records.
376

1	# marvin HDMI → BGRX32 Capture Pipeline
2	
3	Authoritative configuration reference for the 720p60 HDMI capture path on SAM9X75. Every stage, every register bit that matters, with datasheet citations. When something breaks, start here before grepping code.
4	
5	**Status:** working as of 2026-05-02. Validated at **1280×720p60** and **720×480p60**, native BGRX32 in DDR, no CPU post-processing. The pipeline is resolution-agnostic — PFE crop, DMA size, and framebuffer offsets all scale from the TC358743-detected `{width, height}` automatically.
6	
7	Datasheet references are to **SAM9X7 Series DS60001813** (sections 48 = MIPI CSI / D-PHY, 49 = CSI2DC, 50 = ISC). TC358743 refs are to the Toshiba datasheet + mainline Linux `drivers/media/i2c/tc358743.c`.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Pipeline overview
12	
13	```
14	HDMI source (Pi 720p60 RGB)
15	        │
16	        ▼
17	TC358743 HDMI-to-CSI-2 bridge
18	  DT=0x24 RGB888, 2 lanes, 972 Mbps/lane, continuous-clock mode
19	        │
20	        ▼                          <── MIPI CSI-2 D-PHY
21	SAM9X75 DWC D-PHY RX Gen3
22	  HSFREQRANGE=0x0A (950–1000 Mbps band)
23	        │
24	        ▼                          <── 40-bit isc_data bus
25	CSI2DC (Demultiplexer Controller)
26	  VPCFGR: DT=0x24, VC=0, PA=0, RMS=0
27	  → demux_data = 0x00_00RRGGBB, one pixel per VP word
28	        │
29	        ▼                          <── 40-bit vp_data bus
30	ISC — Parallel Front End (PFE)
31	  PFE_CFG0: MIPI=1, BPS=FORTY, MODE=PROGRESSIVE, CONT=1, COLEN=1, ROWEN=1
32	  PFE_CFG1: COLMIN=0, COLMAX=W-1   (1279)
33	  PFE_CFG2: ROWMIN=0, ROWMAX=H-1   (719)
34	        │
35	        ▼                          <── sub420_data[39:0] (unmodified through ISC)
36	ISC — Rounding/Limiting/Packing (RLP)
37	  RLP_CFG: MODE=BYPASS (15)
38	  → rlp_data[31:0] = sub420_data[31:0] = 0x00RRGGBB
39	        │
40	        ▼                          <── rlp_data[31:0]
41	ISC — DMA Host
42	  DCFG: IMODE=PACKED32, YMBSIZE=BEATS32, CMBSIZE=BEATS32
43	  → stores 32-bit words to DDR; little-endian = B G R 00 = BGRX32
44	        │
45	        ▼
46	DDR3 framebuffer  (1280 × 720 × 4 = 3,686,400 B/frame)
47	  B G R 00  B G R 00  B G R 00  ...
48	```
49	
50	---
```

```text
109	### 2.4 CSI2DC — the RMS=0 lever
110	
111	**This is the key decision that enables in-pipeline BGRX32.** DS60001813 §49.6.54:
112	
113	| VPCFGR Field | Value | Reason |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| DT (bits 5:0) | 0x24 | RGB888 (matches TC358743 emission) |
116	| VC (bits 7:6) | 0 | Virtual channel 0 |
117	| PA (bit 14) | **0** | LSB-aligned. PA=1 is for 10/12-bit Bayer sensors being packed onto ISC's 12-bit internal bus. Irrelevant for MIPI RGB888 bypass. |
118	| **RMS (bit 13)** | **0** | **Critical.** See below. |
119	| RGB36MAP (bit 15) | 0 | Use Table 49.25 pixel mapping |
120	
121	`RMS` (Recommended Memory Storage) per datasheet:
122	
123	- `RMS=0` — "CSI2DC outputs 1 pixel per component per clock cycle, compliant with the ISC processing engine." → Table 49.25: `demux_data[39:24]=0`, `[23:16]=R`, `[15:8]=G`, `[7:0]=B`. **One pixel per 40-bit VP word.**
124	- `RMS=1` — "CSI2DC generates a byte stream compliant with the CSI-2 specification memory format." → Table 49.27: 4 BGR pixels packed into 12 bytes. This is what MCC's default config produces — results in **dense 3 B/pixel BGR** (not what we want for direct display).
125	
126	**MCC hardcodes RMS=1.** We override it:
127	
128	```c
129	// firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/csi2dc/plib_csi2dc.c
130	void CSI2DC_Configure_VideoPipe(uint32_t dt, uint32_t vc, uint32_t align_isc) {
131	    CSI2DC_REGS->CSI2DC_VPCFGR = CSI2DC_VPCFGR_DT(dt)
132	                               | CSI2DC_VPCFGR_VC(vc)
133	                               | (align_isc ? CSI2DC_VPCFGR_PA_1 : 0);
134	    /* NOTE: do NOT OR in CSI2DC_VPCFGR_RMS_1 — we want RMS=0 so each pixel
135	     *       occupies a full 40-bit VP word with the low 32 bits = 0x00RRGGBB. */
136	}
137	```
138	
139	Other CSI2DC config:
140	- `GCFGR.MIPIFRN = 0` (free-running, matches TC358743's continuous-clock mode). MCC default is gated (`MIPIFRN=1`); mismatch leaves `CSI2DC.GSR.ARSTIP` stuck on reset. Override via `csi2dcObj->enableMIPIFreeRun = true;` in `isc_capture.c:91`.
141	- `VPER = 1` (video pipe enabled).
142	
143	### 2.5 ISC — Parallel Front End (PFE)
144	
145	DS60001813 §50.6.6, §50.7.4–50.7.6.
146	
147	Key settings configured by `DRV_ISC_Configure()`:
148	
149	| PFE_CFG0 field | Value | Why |
150	|---|---|---|
151	| REP | 0 | N/A for BPS=FORTY |
152	| BPS (30:28) | 5 = FORTY | "40-bit input (used for MIPI formats up to forty bits per pixel)." Matches CSI2DC's 40-bit VP bus. |
153	| MIPI (bit 14) | 1 | Input from MIPI interface |
154	| GATED (bit 8) | 0 | Free-running clock |
155	| CCIR656 (bit 9) | 0 | Not embedded-sync — using MIPI |
156	| CONT (bit 7) | 1 | Continuous acquisition (vs single shot) |
157	| MODE (6:4) | 0 = PROGRESSIVE | Source is progressive |
158	| VPOL / HPOL | 0 | Active-high sync (standard) |
159	
160	**Two bits that MCC leaves OFF but we must set:**
161	
162	| PFE_CFG0 field | Value | Why MCC misses it |
163	|---|---|---|
164	| **COLEN (bit 12)** | **1** | Enables the column crop window |
165	| **ROWEN (bit 13)** | **1** | Enables the row crop window |
166	
167	MCC's `ISC_PFE_Crop_Area()` function is defined in `plib_isc.c` but **never called**. Without COLEN+ROWEN and valid COLMAX/ROWMAX, the PFE expects a 1×1 frame and fires HDTO (Horizontal Detection Timeout) on the first real line. The Linux `mchp-isc` driver sets both bits; we match that.
168	
169	We program these directly after `DRV_ISC_Configure()`:
170	
171	```c
172	// isc_capture.c:204-209
173	ISC_REGS->ISC_PFE_CFG1 = ISC_PFE_CFG1_COLMIN(0u)
174	                       | ISC_PFE_CFG1_COLMAX((uint32_t)width - 1u);   // 1279 at 720p
175	ISC_REGS->ISC_PFE_CFG2 = ISC_PFE_CFG2_ROWMIN(0u)
176	                       | ISC_PFE_CFG2_ROWMAX((uint32_t)height - 1u);  // 719  at 720p
177	ISC_REGS->ISC_PFE_CFG0 |= ISC_PFE_CFG0_COLEN_1 | ISC_PFE_CFG0_ROWEN_1;
178	```
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
208	
209	| DCFG field | Value | Reason |
210	|---|---|---|
211	| **IMODE (2:0)** | **2 = PACKED32** | "32 bits, single channel packed." Stores each `rlp_data[31:0]` as 4 contiguous bytes in memory. Little-endian → `B G R 00`. |
212	| YMBSIZE (6:4) | 4 = BEATS32 | 32-beat AXI burst (sama7g5 / SAM9X7 — MCC's PACKED8 default is BEATS8 which is the sama5d2 value, undersized for this SoC). |
213	| CMBSIZE (10:8) | 4 = BEATS32 | Same rationale as YMBSIZE. |
214	| ARQOS / AWQOS | 0 | Dynamic QoS based on FIFO level (recommended default) |
215	
216	MCC's `DRV_ISC_Configure` sets PACKED8 + BEATS8 if `iscObj->layout = ISC_LAYOUT_PACKED8`. We override after `DRV_ISC_Configure`:
217	
218	```c
219	// isc_capture.c:219-221
220	ISC_REGS->ISC_DCFG = ISC_DCFG_IMODE_PACKED32
221	                   | ISC_DCFG_YMBSIZE_BEATS32
222	                   | ISC_DCFG_CMBSIZE_BEATS32;
223	```
224	
225	The write is safe because nothing in MCC writes DCFG again after this point (the redundant-call to `DRV_ISC_Configure_DMA` was removed). `DRV_ISC_Configure` already calls it internally at `drv_isc.c:381` — don't add a second call.
226	
227	**Descriptor view:** `DCTRL.DVIEW = 0` (PACKED / single channel). `DAD0` holds the current buffer base address. `DST0` = 0 (contiguous frame, no row stride gap).
228	
229	### 2.8 Framebuffer layout in DDR
230	
231	```c
232	// isc_capture.c:17-29
233	#define ISC_CAP_MAX_W        1920u
234	#define ISC_CAP_MAX_H        1080u
235	#define ISC_CAP_BPP          4u      /* BGRX32 */
236	#define ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS  2u
237	
238	static __attribute__((__section__(".region_cache_aligned")))
239	       __attribute__((__aligned__(32)))
240	       uint8_t g_framebuffer[ISC_CAP_MAX_W * ISC_CAP_MAX_H * ISC_CAP_BPP * ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS];
241	```
242	
243	- Pool size: 1920×1080×4×2 = 16.6 MB, in the cacheable DDR region.
244	- 32-byte aligned (cache line boundary for ARM926 L1).
245	- At 720p: only 3,686,400 B × 2 = 7.37 MB actually used.
246	- Double-buffered for tear-free consumption by the display stage (ISR toggles `frameIndex`; probe reads the *previous* completed buffer).
247
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Guitar Hero Bot
2	
3	An autonomous robot that plays Guitar Hero / Rock Band on a Nintendo Wii by watching the game video, detecting notes in real time, and pressing the buttons on a real Wii guitar controller.
4	
5	The system is built around a SAM9X75 host (**marvin**) that captures HDMI directly off the Wii, runs reference computer-vision note detection, schedules chord and strum timing, and sends fret/strum commands over UART to a small actuator MCU (**fretboard**) that drives the controller's buttons via open-drain GPIO. A separate Python tool (**fret-tuner**) is used at the bench for calibration and detector tuning, but is not in the runtime path.
6	
7	For the full system overview see [SPEC.md](SPEC.md).
8	
9	## Where to start

15	| Work on the actuator MCU (sensors, GPIO output) | [firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md](firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md) |
16	| Tune detection algorithms at the bench | [tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md](tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md) |
17	| Work on actuator mechanical / PCB / 3D-print parts | [hardware/](hardware/) |

```text
1	# Guitar Hero Bot — System Specification
2	
3	> Top-level overview. For implementation detail of any single subproject, follow the pointers in §3. Each subproject owns its own spec; this document does not duplicate them.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Mission
8	
9	Build an autonomous robot that plays Guitar Hero / Rock Band on a real Wii guitar controller by watching the game video, detecting notes in real time, and pressing physical buttons in sync with the music. The system must run end-to-end without a host PC in the runtime path, produce reference-quality detector output that lighter detectors can be trained against, and provide an on-device operator UI for calibration, mode control, and replay.
10	
11	## 2. Current architecture
12	
13	Three pieces, one runtime brain:
14	
15	```
16	Wii ──HDMI──► ElectronWarp ──HDMI──► TC358743 ──CSI-2──┐
17	                                                       ▼
18	   ┌──────────────────────  marvin (SAM9X75)  ────────────┐
19	   │  HDMI capture → CV detect → timing pipeline → cmds   │
20	   │           ↑              detector-state bus          │
21	   │           │                       ▲                  │
22	   │           │  10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch │                  │
23	   │           │       (operator UI)    │                  │
24	   │           └────────── SD card ─────┘  (recording)    │
25	   └────────┬──────────────────────────┬───────────────────┘
26	            │ UART cmds (frets/strum)  │ UART (raw ADC)
27	            ▼                          │
28	   ┌──────────────────────────────────┐│
29	   │   fretboard (PIC32CM6408)        │┘
30	   │   ADC scan ↔ open-drain GPIO     │
31	   └────────┬─────────────────────────┘
32	            │ GPIO
33	            ▼
34	   Wii guitar controller ──► Wii (closes the loop)
35	
36	                ◇ off-band: dev PC running fret-tuner
37	                  (calibration / detector tuning / replay)
38	```
39	
40	**Per-tier role summary:**
41	
42	- **marvin** — SAM9X75 Curiosity host. Owns HDMI capture, the *reference* CV note detector, ingest of fretboard ADC samples, the chord/strum timing pipeline, command emission to fretboard, the on-device LVDS+touch operator UI, and reference-data recording to SD. The runtime brain.
43	- **fretboard** — PIC32CM6408PL10048 MCU on a sensor/actuator board. Streams 5-channel phototransistor ADC up to marvin and converts incoming bitmask commands into open-drain GPIO presses on a Wii guitar controller. Has a standalone fallback mode where it runs its own chord FIFO without marvin in the loop.
44	- **fret-tuner** — Off-band Python tool (FastAPI + browser UI, Linux/macOS PC). Used at the bench for sensor calibration, detector-algorithm tuning, and replay analysis of recordings produced by marvin. Not in the runtime path.
45	
46	## 3. Subproject specs (where detail lives)
47	
48	| Subproject | Spec | Journal |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| marvin | [`firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) | [`firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md) |
51	| fretboard | [`firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`](firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md) | — |
52	| fret-tuner | [`tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md`](tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md) | — |
53	
54	marvin's spec also has deeper-dive documents for its capture and display paths ([`capture_pipeline.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/capture_pipeline.md), [`display_path.md`](firmware/marvin/docs/display_path.md)).
55	
56	## 4. Repository map
57	
58	```
59	guitar-pic/
60	├── README.md                    # short landing page
61	├── SPEC.md                      # this document
62	├── CLAUDE.md                    # workflow rules for Claude Code sessions
63	├── firmware/
64	│   ├── marvin/                  # SAM9X75 host firmware
65	│   ├── fretboard/               # PIC32CM6408 sensor/actuator MCU firmware
66	│   └── sam9x75_curiosity_emirror/   # Microchip reference project (template only)
67	├── tools/
68	│   └── fret-tuner/              # Python dev/calibration tool
69	├── hardware/
70	│   ├── actuators/               # voice coil / electromagnet / DIY solenoid design + test protocols
71	│   ├── 3d-models/               # OpenSCAD + STL for printed actuator parts
72	│   ├── Sensor-LCD5/             # KiCad project for fretboard sensor/actuator PCB
73	│   └── kicad/                   # shared symbol/footprint libraries
74	└── docs/
75	    ├── SAM9X7-Series-Data-Sheet-DS60001813.pdf
76	    └── archive/                 # historical docs from the original PC/Elgato/PS2 architecture
77	```
78	
79	## 5. Hardware platforms (high-level)
80	
81	| Component | Role | Where to look |
82	|---|---|---|
83	| SAM9X75 Curiosity | marvin host | [marvin spec §3](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md) |
84	| Waveshare HDMI→CSI-2 adapter (TC358743) | HDMI bridge into marvin | [marvin spec §3](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md), [capture pipeline](firmware/marvin/docs/capture_pipeline.md) |
85	| 10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch | marvin operator UI surface | [marvin display path](firmware/marvin/docs/display_path.md) |
86	| Sensor/actuator PCB (Sensor-LCD5) | fretboard board: 5 phototransistors + GPIO out | [`hardware/Sensor-LCD5/`](hardware/Sensor-LCD5/) |
87	| PIC32CM6408PL10048 | fretboard MCU | [fretboard spec](firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md) |
88	| Actuator mechanism (TBD: voice coil / electromagnet / DIY solenoid) | physical fret + strum drive | [`hardware/actuators/`](hardware/actuators/) and [`hardware/3d-models/`](hardware/3d-models/) |
89	| ElectronWarp | component → HDMI converter for Wii | external commercial part |
90	
91	The actuator choice is intentionally still open — `hardware/actuators/` contains design + test-protocol docs for three candidates.
92	
93	## 6. Cross-cutting decisions
94	
95	- **Architecture pivot.** The original PC-hosted / Elgato-USB-capture / PS2 / single-PIC-actuator design is retired. Source documents are preserved at [`docs/archive/`](docs/archive/) for design-rationale reference; they are *not* maintained.
96	- **`frame_epoch` is the master sync token.** A 32-bit counter incremented by marvin's video task on every captured ISC frame. Every detector-state record, emitted command, and recording artifact — including data from off-board observers — keys off this token so multi-source data can be aligned post-hoc. Detail in [marvin spec §4.6](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md).
97	- **Reference data persists on marvin's SD card.** Detector-state + sparse raw-BGRX32 keyframes (default 1 keyframe/sec) + raw ADC stream + emitted commands. Off-board detectors record their own data keyed by `frame_epoch` and align offline.
98	- **Centralized timing on marvin, with a fretboard-takeover fallback.** marvin runs the chord-window FIFO and strum scheduler by default; an operator-mode toggle hands timing back to fretboard's standalone `fret_button.c` while marvin still records observations.
99	- **Operating modes are independent toggles**, not a global state machine: `detect_enable`, `marvin_timing_enable`, `actuate_enable`, `record_enable`. Named modes (idle / calibrate / dry-run / play / replay / record) are presets over them.
100	
101	## 7. Project-wide phasing
102	
103	| Status | Item |
104	|---|---|
105	| ✅ | marvin HDMI capture → DDR (BGRX32) at 480p60 and 720p60 |
106	| ✅ | marvin DDR → 10.1″ LVDS panel display (pillarboxed/letterboxed) |
107	| ✅ | marvin FreeRTOS scheduler + video task split |
108	| ✅ | fretboard standalone play (phototransistors + open-drain GPIO) |
109	| ✅ | fret-tuner used at the bench for detector tuning |
110	| 🚧 | **M1** — marvin reference detector v0 (one CV detector publishing onto the detector-state bus) |
111	| 🚧 | **M2** — fretboard ↔ marvin UART link (ADC ingest + command TX) |
112	| 🚧 | **M3** — end-to-end play (marvin commands actuating through fretboard) |
113	| 🚧 | **M4** — recording-to-SD (detector-state + keyframes + ADC + commands) |
114	| 🚧 | **M5** — operator UI v0 (live view + mode toggles) |
115	| 🚧 | **M6**+ — calibration UI, replay, fretboard-takeover validation |
116	
117	Detail (definitions of done, demos) in [marvin spec §8](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md).
118	
119	## 8. What this is *not*
120	
121	To anchor against the original architecture (preserved in `docs/archive/`):
122	
123	- **Not PC-hosted.** marvin is the runtime brain; no host PC is required for play.
124	- **Not USB-capture / Elgato.** Video is captured directly off HDMI via a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 path into the SAM9X75's ISC.
125	- **Not PS2.** The supported console is the Nintendo Wii (with an ElectronWarp component → HDMI converter).
126	- **Not a single-MCU actuator.** Sensing and timing live on marvin; fretboard is a sensor/actuator MCU, not a solo controller (with the explicit exception of the standalone-fallback mode).
127	- **Not OpenCV / Python at runtime.** CV runs natively on the SAM9X75 (Cortex-A5). Python (`fret-tuner`) is a bench tool only.
128	
129	## 9. License & acknowledgments
130	
131	MIT License — see `LICENSE` if present.
132	
133	Hobby / educational project for learning computer vision and embedded systems. Guitar Hero and Rock Band are trademarks of Activision and Harmonix respectively. Wii is a trademark of Nintendo.
134
```

1	# Project rules
2	
3	These rules apply to every session on this repo. Follow them without being reminded.
4	
5	## Specs orient you; journals track progress
6	
7	The repo has three subprojects (marvin, fretboard, fret-tuner) plus a top-level system spec.
8	
9	- **[`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md) is the cross-subproject overview** — read it first if a task spans subprojects or if you're new to the repo. It points at each subproject's spec and journal.
10	- For non-trivial work inside a single subproject, read that subproject's spec **and** journal first (see below).
11	
12	## Journals are the source of truth for planning and progress
13	
14	This repo uses working journals to track planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress *outside* the chat context so they survive across sessions, compactions, and restarts.
15	
16	Current journals:
17	
18	- `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md` — marvin firmware (SAM9X75 vision-based guitar-playing robot)
19	  - System-level spec for marvin lives at `firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md` — **read it first** alongside the journal on any non-trivial marvin task. The spec is the durable description of what marvin is (purpose, subsystems, interfaces, milestones); the journal is the running diary.
20	
21	When working on a subproject that has a journal:
22	
23	1. **Read the journal first.** Before responding to any non-trivial request, read the journal for that subproject. It contains the current focus, phased plan, open questions, decision log, and session log — the state you need to be useful.
24	2. **Update the journal as you go.** When we make a decision, resolve an open question, finish a plan phase, or finish a session, reflect that in the journal. Newest entries at the top within each section.
25	   - Decisions → append to the decision log with date and rationale.
26	   - Resolved open questions → remove from "Open questions" and add to the decision log with the answer and rationale.
27	   - Plan progress → check off phase items; add sub-bullets for anything learned during implementation.
28	   - Session close → add a dated session-log entry summarizing what happened.
29	3. **Prefer updating the journal over restating plans in chat.** If I'd otherwise write a multi-paragraph plan in chat, it belongs in the journal — the chat is ephemeral, the journal isn't.
30	4. **If a new subproject needs a journal, create one** using the same structure as `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`, and add it to the list above in this file.
31	
32	## Code comments describe current code only
33	
34	Comments in source files explain **what the code currently does and why**, when that's non-obvious. They are not a development diary.
35	
36	Do not put any of the following in source comments — they belong in the journal, commit messages, or PR descriptions:
37	
38	- Narrative of how the code evolved ("previously we did X, now we do Y", "this replaces the old …")
39	- Debug notes, troubleshooting history, or why something *doesn't* work
40	- TODO lists for future features (use the journal or an issue tracker)
41	- References to tasks, tickets, or past conversations ("fix for Greg's bug", "see chat from 2026-05-01")
42	- Extensive block comments explaining design rationale — a one-line "why" is fine; multi-paragraph prose goes in the journal
43	
44	**Default to no comment.** Only add one when removing it would confuse a future reader. If you catch yourself wanting to write a paragraph, write it in the journal instead and link from the code if needed (e.g. `// see firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`).
45

10	Do not commit to the repo on your own initiative. Only run `git commit` when the user explicitly asks for it, or when prompting them first about something that genuinely needs to be captured.
11	
12	**Why:** Greg prefers to control commit boundaries himself. Auto-committing every change makes the history noisy and mixes my interpretation of "milestone" with his actual thinking about when work is ready to land.
13	
14	**How to apply:**
15	- After making edits, stop. Don't stage, don't commit.
16	- If something seems important enough to capture (e.g., a working state worth preserving before further experimentation), surface it as a question/suggestion: "Want me to commit this?" rather than acting.
17	- Stage-only (`git add`) is fine when explicitly requested or as a setup step before a user-approved commit.
18	- This applies to all repos in the workspace, not just one.
